mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: In a rising rate regime, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 70% of such trigger months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as inflation expectations cool.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >50,000 jobs in a month
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive months of such labor growth spikes, the 20-day forward return remains negative or flat.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month moving average, the S&P 60-day forward return turns negative due to weakening economic momentum.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in at least 80% of similar 60-day windows since the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales (not available) and housing starts (not available) proxies would be ideal, but using HOUST (residential construction) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) jointly, a positive correlation predicts a positive S&P 20-day return when both are above trend.
regime_hint: Dual demand indicators above trend in QoQ growth
failure_condition: The joint signal shows no significant correlation with 20-day forward returns in out-of-sample tests (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a negative S&P 60-day forward return as market anticipates a tightening labor market.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% in a month
failure_condition: Over 12 months of such triggers, the 60-day forward return remains non-negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) with no reversal for 6 months, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as discounting effects favor equities.
failure_condition: In 10 such 6-month rate-cutting regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically superior to a flat market (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (not available) diverge with INDPRO falling while GDP momentum proxies (not available) remain stable, the S&P 60-day forward return turns negative due to supply-side imbalance.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines while 12-month moving average remains steady for 2 months
regime_hint: Discrepancy between production and momentum indicators
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly different from zero in 8 out of 10 such imbalance events.
